blocks.text: Different cutaneous receptors (receptors of the skin) respond to touch, pressure, heat, cold, and pain.

Nociceptors detect pain. Pain is defined as a stimulus that causes or is about to cause tissue damage. Nociceptors consist of free nerve endings located throughout the body, especially near surfaces. Different nociceptors may respond to extremes in temperature, very intense pressure, or specific chemicals (including some that are released by injured cells).

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text:
Thermoreceptors: are naked dendrite endings of sensory neurons. They detect fall and rise in temperature. Cold receptors are located immediately below the epidermis, while warm receptors are located slightly deeper, in the dermis.
Thermoreceptors are also found within the hypothalamus of the brain, where they detect the temperature of the blood and thus monitor the body’s internal (core) temperature.
The skin contains a variety of touch receptors. They are mechanoreceptors that respond to different physical stimuli.

items: Meissner's corpuscles are endings of sensory neurons surrounded by a capsule. They are found in the upper layer of the skin (especially in lips, fingertips, palm, and soles). They detect light touch and vibration.
Hair follicle receptors are endings of neurons and are located around the base of hair follicles. They detect the movement of hairs, which occur due to mechanical or thermal stimuli.
Merkel cells are oval-shaped receptors in the deepest layer of epidermis. They detect light touch and are present in highly touch-sensitive areas like fingertips.
Pacinian corpuscles are sensory neuron endings, surrounded by a capsule. They are located deeper in the skin. They detect deep pressure and vibration.
Ruffini endings are also sensory neuron endings enclosed in capsule. They are located in the dermis. They detect sustained pressure and stretching.

blocks.alt: A block of skin with the epidermis, the dermis and the fat layer. A hair runs through the epidermis into its follicle, with hair follicle receptors wrapped round its base. Free nerve endings reach into the epidermis, Merkel cells sit at the base of the epidermis, a Meissner corpuscle lies in the upper dermis, a Ruffini ending deeper in the dermis and a Pacinian corpuscle in the fat layer, all joined to a sensory nerve.

blocks.long_description: Labels: Free nerve endings (pain, heat, cold), Merkel cells (touch), Hair follicle receptors (touch & movement), Meissner corpuscle (touch), Ruffini endings (pressure & stretching), Pacinian corpuscle (pressure).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 15.19 labels 'Markel cells'; the correct name is Merkel cells, as drawn above.
These touch receptors generate and transmit impulses via sensory neurons to the spinal cord and then to brain, where the signals are processed to create the sensations of touch.
